clue.text: It's mainly green as opposed to the 15 one

definitions.text: It's mainly green as opposed to the 15 one

parts.words: It's mainly green as opposed to the 15 one
parts.note: on the main (the open sea) a ship shows a green navigation lamp on its right-hand side, set against the red lamp on the left side named by 15

explanation.surface: A remark on a colour being mostly green, in contrast with another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'mostly' but means 'on the main', at sea. 15 is PORT, so the clue contrasts the green lamp on a ship's right side with the red one on its left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships at night carry a green lamp on the right-hand side and a red lamp on the left, so the right-side navigation lamp is green.

clue.text: Fencing with leader of setters over puns?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of setters is taken

parts.note: puns are a form of wordplay

explanation.surface: A crossword setter ponders whether duelling with puns counts as a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the S above WORDPLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing is the sport of combat with blades, which is exactly what this term describes.

clue.text: A sort of 11 snake

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters of the 11 across answer are rearranged

parts.note: 11 points to the answer of 11 across, meaning was bold

explanation.surface: A reference to a variety of snake connected with another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is a link word; the anagram uses the 11 across answer, DARED.
explanation.definitionFit: The common European viper, Britain's only venomous serpent, goes by this name.

clue.text: Helping of husks makes us flourish

parts.note: bran is the husks of grain separated from flour
a dish is a helping or serving of food

explanation.surface: A bowl of cereal husks gives us a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping of husks' is a bowl of husks, read in answer order as husks then the bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave a weapon about showily is to flourish it.

clue.text: Sort of well set up in a rain storm

indicators.note: in places the turned-round word inside the rearranged letters
a storm throws things into turmoil, so the letters of a rain are jumbled
in a down clue, up means the word set is read from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: A well is dug during a rainstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' gives TES, which goes inside ARIAN, the shuffle of A RAIN signalled by 'storm'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps groundwater under pressure, so water rises without pumping.

clue.text: Fly ship's cook ?

definitions.meaning: an angler's artificial fly, as in the salmon fly called the Silver ...
old nautical slang for the cook aboard a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a salmon-fishing lure and, in sailors' slang, the man who cooks in the galley.

clue.text: See 1
What a 13 is to the 9

parts.note: 13 is a man who lives ashore and 9 is a seasoned sailor; the contemptuous word sailors use for a clumsy non-sailor is wanted

explanation.surface: How one character in the puzzle is regarded by another.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is LANDSMAN and 9 is OLD SALT; to an old sailor a landsman is a clumsy, unseamanlike fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' term of scorn for an awkward novice or anyone unused to the sea.

clue.text: Turkish port's bitterness over one penny on change of oil

parts.note: gall is bitterness of spirit
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a change of the letters of oil means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Turkish harbour's sourness is set against a penny and an oil change.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' and 'on' simply stack the pieces in order: GALL, I, P, then OLI from 'change of oil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli (Gelibolu) is a harbour town on the Dardanelles peninsula in Turkey.

clue.text: Compact arrangement of trees

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of trees puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Trees laid out tightly in a garden plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact speech is brief and succinct, using few words.

clue.text: Ancient mariner a long time in the cellar?

definitions.meaning: a veteran sailor who has been at sea for years

definitions.text: a long time in the cellar?
definitions.meaning: salt left in its salt cellar for ages is aged salt

explanation.definitionFit: An experienced seaman is called this, and the cellar is the salt cellar, whose contents have been there a long time.

clue.text: He patches things up with an iced drink

definitions.meaning: a mender of shoes who patches and resoles them
a sherry ... is a drink of wine, sugar and fruit over crushed ice

explanation.surface: A handyman serves a cold drink with his repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a shoe-mender and an iced drink of wine with fruit and sugar.

clue.text: Was bold when challenged

definitions.meaning: had the courage to do something
issued a challenge to someone to do something

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb means both ventured boldly and invited someone to prove their nerve.

clue.text: Here lions cause havoc at the seaside

indicators.note: lions causing havoc throw things into disorder, so the letters of here lions are mixed up

explanation.surface: Lions run riot at a beach resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge where land meets sea is the seaside or coast.

clue.text: His is not the sea side of any 12

definitions.text: His is not the sea side of any 12

parts.words: His is not the sea side of any 12
parts.note: 12 is the boundary of land and sea; the person wanted belongs on the land side of it, not the water side

explanation.surface: A man described by which side of a coastline he keeps to.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is SHORELINE; a man who keeps to the land side of it is no sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old nautical usage for someone who lives and works ashore rather than at sea.

clue.text: Novel knitwear supplied by the State ?

parts.note: novel means new
a jersey is a knitted pullover

explanation.surface: Fresh sweaters are handed out by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The State' reads as the government but is a US state; a jersey is British for a knitted sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Wine with 6 ac is red

definitions.meaning: the lamp on a ship's left side, joined with the 6 across word, shows red

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Portuguese fortified wine and the left side of a ship, whose navigation lamp is red.

clue.text: Puts up with bad stereo alt

indicators.note: bad means faulty or spoilt, so the letters of stereo alt are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone endures a poor-quality stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting up with something means bearing or enduring it.

clue.text: What exaggeration makes out of a 20

definitions.text: What exaggeration makes out of a 20

parts.words: What exaggeration makes out of a 20
parts.note: 20 is the little heap a burrowing animal throws up; the idiom of overstatement turns it into something huge

explanation.surface: What overstatement does to a small thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is MOLEHILL: to exaggerate is to make a mountain out of a molehill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for overstatement is blowing a small matter up into a towering peak.

clue.text: Half, not one, school for girls

parts.note: semi is the prefix meaning half
nary means not one, as in nary a word

explanation.surface: A girls' school is half empty, without a single pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage a seminary was a private boarding school, especially one for young ladies.

clue.text: The boat left way back

indicators.note: back means the letters of left and way are read in reverse

explanation.surface: The boat departed by the rear route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the whole of L plus WAY round.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Rise of the underground worker

parts.note: the mole is an animal that digs tunnels under the soil
a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A promotion for someone who works below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like a promotion for a miner, but it is a hill, and the worker is a burrowing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The small heap of earth a burrowing mole throws up is its own little hill.

clue.text: Like 9's hand that held the wedding-guest

definitions.text: Like 9's hand that held the wedding-guest

parts.words: Like 9's hand that held the wedding-guest
parts.note: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner: the old sailor stops a man going to a wedding and grips him with a bony, thin hand

explanation.surface: Describing the hand an old sailor used to detain a wedding guest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner: 'He holds him with his skinny hand.' 9 is OLD SALT, standing for the mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem describes the mariner's grip with this word for very thin and bony.

clue.text: Hence three wise men bowled over at sea

definitions.text: Hence three wise men bowled over at sea

parts.words: Hence three wise men bowled over at sea
parts.note: a nursery rhyme tells of three wise men of a certain English village who went to sea in a bowl; the place they came from is wanted

explanation.surface: Three sages are knocked over on a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three wise men' suggests the Magi, but the rhyme is 'Three wise men of Gotham went to sea in a bowl'; 'bowled' means sailing in a bowl and 'Hence' asks where they came from.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme names this Nottinghamshire village as home of the three wise men who sailed in a bowl.

clue.text: Might possibly be dark now before this gang repairs it

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of be dark now may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A warning that night may fall before the repair crew fixes things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' is a link word; the fodder is BE DARK NOW. A breakdown gang is a railway crew sent to clear a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical failure is what exists before the repair crew arrives to put it right.

clue.text: Railway law-breaking causes noisy quarrel

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the old national railway

indicators.note: breaking the letters of law shatters them into a new order

explanation.surface: Lawbreaking on the railway leads to a loud dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Railways, Britain's state rail network.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rowdy fight or noisy row.

clue.text: Bury in Tintern Abbey

indicators.note: in signals the answer is concealed inside the word Tintern

explanation.surface: A burial at Tintern Abbey, a ruined monastery in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintern Abbey is a ruined Cistercian abbey in the Wye valley in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury someone is to inter them in a grave.

clue.text: Friendly group's two-wheeler

definitions.meaning: the Friendly Islands, the Pacific archipelago named so by Captain Cook
a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of India

explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific kingdom once called the Friendly Islands shares its name with a two-wheeled Indian cart.

clue.text: Sailors in th' drink!

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, so ABS are sailors
th' is an old clipped form of the, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors have fallen into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In th' drink' suggests sailors overboard; 'drink' is the definition, an aniseed spirit, here in the old spelling without a final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green spirit flavoured with wormwood and anise.

clue.text: Opposed to a lasting improvement, lacking money

indicators.note: an improvement reworks something, so the remaining letters are reordered
lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, the sign for money

explanation.surface: Someone is against an improvement that would last, given the lack of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: From A LASTING remove L (pound, from Latin libra), and rearrange AASTING, signalled by 'improvement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means being in opposition to it.

clue.text: Store at the roadside?

definitions.meaning: to save or put aside for the future
a parking place beside the road where drivers can pull in

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to save up, and as one word it is a roadside pull-in for vehicles.

clue.text: Rich man in Shylock's dream

definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice Shylock says he did dream of sacks of cash last night

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a wealthy person, and Shylock says 'I did dream of money-bags to-night'.
